resources.string: Shown instead from %1$s to %2$s. Change the hours under Night.
Same as day. Open a screensaver and tap Use at night.
%1$s is picked. It starts once setup is finished.
Pick a screensaver below, then choose how Beddery starts when your phone is charging.
A big, calm clock with the date, your next alarm and battery status. Clean and easy to read from across the room.
An elegant watch face with a smooth sweeping second hand and today\'s date.
A retro split-flap clock. Each minute the cards flip over just like the real thing.
Tells the time in words, like \"it is twenty past ten\". Dots count the minutes in between. English only.
A dim, deep-red clock on pure black. Gives off almost no light, so it won\'t keep you awake.
Hours, minutes and seconds as glowing binary dots, with the decimal digits underneath if you need a hint.
The time drifts around the screen and changes color at each wall. Will it ever hit the corner?
Watch your battery fill up with a gentle liquid animation, plus how long until it\'s full.
The time, current conditions and the next few hours of forecast, so you know what to wear tomorrow.
The time alongside your upcoming calendar events for today and tomorrow.
Your time plus clocks for the cities you care about, with day and night at a glance.
A slow, cinematic slideshow of photos you choose, with the time in the corner.
A guided breathing circle to help you unwind before sleep. Follow it in and out.
Warm blobs of wax rise, fall and melt into each other.
Fireflies drift and blink over a summer meadow at night.
A miniature solar system with planets circling the sun.
Drifting stars that link up into shifting constellations, in your accent color.
Cascading green glyphs, straight out of a hacker movie.
Conway\'s cellular automaton. Cells are born, live and die. When the world settles down, a new one begins.
Open Beddery and allow calendar access to see your events here.
Nothing on your calendar. Enjoy the quiet.
Open Beddery and add some photos to fill this frame.
Open Beddery to choose a weather location.
Couldn\'t reach the weather service. Will try again soon.
Couldn\'t get your location. Try searching for your city instead.
Allowed. Events from your visible calendars will appear.
Needed to show your events. Beddery only reads them on this phone.
In 4 s, hold 4 s, out 4 s, hold 4 s. Steady and focusing.
In 4 s, hold 7 s, out 8 s. A classic for falling asleep.
In 4 s, out 6 s. Long exhales slow your heart rate.
Recommended. Tap Open, choose Beddery as your screen saver, and set it to start while charging.
Beddery is your screensaver and starts while charging.
Beddery is selected. Make sure \"When to start\" includes while charging.
This phone doesn\'t offer Android\'s screensaver. Use Standby mode instead.
Works on any phone. Shows Beddery over the lock screen when you\'re charging. Tap to close.
Start when the screen turns off
While charging. If you close Beddery, it waits until you unlock or re-plug before showing again.
Single taps won\'t close Beddery, so a bump in the night won\'t either. Works however Beddery starts.
Allow notifications so Beddery can appear on your lock screen.
Allow full-screen notifications so Beddery can take over the lock screen.
Optional: some phones close background apps aggressively. Turning off battery optimization for Beddery keeps Standby reliable.
Show a small clock on screensavers that don\'t have one
Gently move static elements so they don\'t leave marks on OLED screens
Lowest brightness, darker colors and less blue light during your sleep hours
Removes blue and green light, which is easiest on sleepy eyes
Rotate through the ones marked \"In shuffle\", or all of them if none are marked
Shuffle is on. Using just this screensaver turns shuffle off.
No accounts, no ads, no tracking
A polished take on %1$s. Open the full-screen preview and swipe to compare them side by side.
Tip: in full-screen preview, swipe left and right to browse.

plurals.item: Shuffling %1$d screensaver · a new one each time it starts

resources.string: The red LED alarm clock you grew up with: glowing seven-segment digits, a blinking colon and little indicator lamps.
Glowing orange numerals inside glass tubes, with the unlit digits stacked faintly behind.
Mechanical number drums that roll over every second, with a little bounce as each digit settles.
The time as bold, poster-sized type. Heavy hours, light minutes, nothing else.
Hours, minutes and seconds as three smoothly filling rings around the time.
A valley through the whole day. The sun rides an arc from today\'s real sunrise to sunset, the moon takes the night, and the land\'s colours follow the light. Uses your weather location when set.
Album art, the song and play, pause and skip buttons for whatever your phone is playing, in eight styles from a spinning record to a gig poster. Uses notification access.
Play some music and it shows up here.
Allow notification access in Beddery\'s settings to see what\'s playing.
Show Now Playing when music plays
Switches to album art and controls while music plays, and back once it stops
The time and a calm summary of your notifications, grouped by app. You choose whether message content is shown.
How long until your alarm, and how many full sleep cycles that leaves. No alarm? It suggests good times to wake up.
Tonight\'s moon at its true phase in a deep night sky with the Milky Way: its real seas and craters lit in relief, with how much is lit and when it\'s next full.
This month at a glance, with today circled and dots on days with events.
How far through the day, week, month and year you are, plus every day of the year as a dot.
Raindrops gather and trickle down a window, with the city\'s lights glowing softly beyond.
A campfire in a clearing by a mountain lake, with a tent, a lantern and sparks drifting up past the pines. Tap to stoke the fire.
Three candles at an open window on a summer night, with a curtain stirring in the breeze and fireflies outside. Tap to breathe on the flames.
Snow falls over a pine forest at night, and a cabin window glows warm in the distance.
Looking down into a moonlit pond as five koi circle beneath a white lotus and drifting maple leaves. Tap to send out a ripple.
A moon jelly and an amber sea nettle climb and sink through deep blue water, ghosts drift far off, and now and then a far jelly glows in colour. Tap for a flash of light.
Soft fields of color drift and blend. The palette changes every few minutes.
Thousands of particles follow invisible currents, leaving silky trails in your accent color.
A swinging-pendulum drawing machine traces a delicate figure, then starts a new one.
Eighteen pendulums swing in and out of step, making waves and patterns, and line up again every minute.
A soft, glassy orb that fills as you breathe in and empties as you breathe out, with a quiet progress ring. Nothing else.
A textured moon behind drifting clouds, and thousands of tiny sparkles on the swell below.
Fine, shimmering curtains of light over layered mountains, mirrored in a still lake.
Glossy wax lit from below, melting and merging smoothly in a warm glass lamp.
A layered meadow at dusk with fireflies near and far, the closest softly out of focus.
Stars stream past through colorful nebulae, with fading trails and the occasional jump to hyperspace.
A detailed solar system: shaded planets, Saturn\'s rings, an asteroid belt and a turbulent sun.
Stars at different depths link up while tiny signals hop from star to star.
Less than one full sleep cycle left. Rest well.
Fall asleep now and you\'ll wake between sleep cycles at
Notifications are turned off in Beddery\'s settings.
Open Beddery and allow notification access to see them here.
Beddery can start in two ways while your phone charges. You only need one.
Both are on, so Beddery may start twice. We suggest turning one off.
Both show Beddery while your phone charges and keep it locked. The difference is what starts it.
When the screen times out while charging. Android decides when.
The moment you plug in, or when you lock your phone.
Choose Beddery in Android\'s Screen saver settings.
Turn it on here and allow two permissions.
Most phones. Some makers remove it.
A small watcher with a silent notification.
Android screensaver. It\'s built in and needs nothing running in the background. Choose Standby if you\'d like Beddery to appear the moment you plug in.
Standby mode. This phone doesn\'t include Android\'s screensaver, and Standby works everywhere.
Lets clocks and info screens show your notifications. They never leave your phone.
Allowed. Supported screensavers show your notifications.
Shows which apps have new notifications, without any content.
Also shows the sender and message. Anyone near your phone can read them.
Off keeps your sleep hours free of notifications
Silent and ongoing notifications are skipped. Apps that hide their content on your lock screen stay hidden here too.
Built into Android. Starts when the screen times out.
Starts the moment you plug in. Works on every phone.
Choose Beddery as the screen saver
In Android\'s Screen saver settings, pick Beddery.
Under \"When to start\", choose while charging.
Android starts the screensaver once the screen times out while charging. Want Beddery the moment you plug in? Choose Standby instead.
Lets Beddery appear on your lock screen.
Lets Beddery take over the lock screen.
Some phones close background apps. Turning off battery optimization keeps Standby reliable.
Android doesn\'t say whether this is done. Open settings to check.
Opened. Make sure it\'s switched on.
%1$s phones close background apps and block pop-ups more than most. These steps keep Standby working. Menus differ between versions: if a page doesn\'t match, search Settings for the switch\'s name.
Find Beddery in the Autostart list and switch it on, so Standby keeps watching for your charger.
Allow showing on the lock screen
In Other permissions, allow \"Show on Lock screen\" and \"Display pop-up windows while running in the background\".
Set Battery saver to No restrictions
In App info, tap Battery saver and choose No restrictions.
In App info, tap Battery usage and turn on \"Allow background activity\" and \"Allow auto launch\".
If your phone has a separate Auto launch or Startup manager list, switch Beddery on there too.
In App info, tap Battery and allow high background power use. On some phones it\'s under Settings, Battery, Background power consumption.
Find Beddery in the Autostart list and switch it on, so Standby keeps watching for your charger.
Ready. Beddery starts when your screen times out while charging.
Ready. Beddery starts when you plug in.
Almost ready. Check the steps below.
Drifting points link up into an ever-changing geometric web, in your accent color.
Your battery as glowing liquid in a glass vial, bubbling while it charges.
Your charge as one giant number that fills with color from the bottom up.
Watch energy flow up the cable into the battery, faster on a fast charger. Wireless charging shows rings rising from the pad.
A little plant that grows as your phone charges, and blooms when it\'s full.
A big battery made of ten glowing cells, with a light sweeping through the ones still charging.
A very supportive sheep with opinions about how much sleep you\'re about to get. Tap him to see what else he\'s up to.
Follow a dot around a square: breathe in, hold, breathe out, hold, four seconds each.
Breathe with the sea. The tide rises as you breathe in and falls as you breathe out.
Gentle prompts, one at a time, to help your body let go of the day.
Numbers slowly counting down from 100, one per long breath out. A classic way to drift off.
A giant LED globe over a desert city, mirrored in a lake. A smiley that watches passing planes and cars, the moon, a cat, the earth, a snooze and fireworks. Tap for the next show.
Topographic lines over a landscape that slowly shifts and reshapes itself.
Stacked lines rise into mountain ridges that roll slowly towards you.
Breathe out slowly as each number changes
At normal speed, the pendulums line up again every minute.

string-array.name: coach_thrilled
string-array.item: Over nine hours. Who are you?
Look at you, getting real sleep.
An early night. Your future self says thanks.
This is the dream. Literally.
Nine hours? I\'m framing this.
Tomorrow-you is going to be unstoppable.
Sleep like this and you\'ll glow.
Gold star. Now go collect your sleep.
I didn\'t think I\'d see the day.
Champion sleeper, reporting for bed.

string-array.name: coach_happy
string-array.item: A proper night\'s sleep. Off you go.
Perfect amount of sleep. Lights out.
Nicely done. Now put the phone down.
Right on schedule. Sweet dreams.
This is the way. Pillow time.
Good timing. The bed\'s warm.
Solid night ahead. Don\'t waste it.
You\'ve earned this one. Sleep well.
Eight-ish hours. The sheep approve.
Teeth brushed? Then bed.

string-array.name: coach_meh
string-array.item: Hmm. That\'s cutting it close.
Your future self is taking notes.
Still time to salvage this. Bed.
Not great, not terrible. Bed now.
One more scroll costs you a dream.
Six-ish hours. We can do better.
Close the tabs. All of them.
The pillow is waiting. Patiently.
Tomorrow\'s alarm is not your friend.
Let\'s not make this a habit.

string-array.name: coach_disappointed
string-array.item: The sheep are disappointed. All of them.
Tomorrow\'s coffee is already nervous.
I\'m not mad. I\'m just… counting.
This is going to be a long morning.
Please. For me. Go to sleep.
Even the moon is judging you.
Your eyelids called. They\'re tired.
Five hours is a nap with ambition.
I believed in you.
Every minute counts now. Bed.

string-array.name: coach_panic
string-array.item: It is late. It is SO late.
Go. To. Sleep.
Sleep is a lesson you\'ll learn tomorrow.
Put. The. Phone. Down.
Your alarm is closer than you think.
This is not a drill.
Bed. Now. I\'m serious.
Tomorrow\'s you is filing a complaint.
Three hours. Make them count.
Why are we still awake?

string-array.name: coach_frantic
string-array.item: This is fine. Everything is fine.
Under two hours. I have melted.
I can hear the alarm from here.
Is it even worth it? Yes. Go.
Any sleep is better than no sleep.
I\'ve stopped counting sheep. I\'m one of them.
Close your eyes. Just try.
Coffee will not save you.
I\'m too tired to be mad.
Lie down. Right now. Anywhere.

string-array.name: coach_no_alarm
string-array.item: No alarm? Bold strategy.
No alarm set. Living dangerously, I see.
Sleeping in? I\'ll just be here. Judging.
No alarm. The world is your snooze.
Free tomorrow? Sleep anyway.
No alarm means no excuses.
Treat yourself to a long one.
The bed\'s open all night.
No rush. But also, bed.
Enjoy the lie-in. You\'ve earned it.

string-array.name: wind_down_prompts
string-array.item: Let your shoulders drop.
Unclench your jaw.
Soften the space between your eyes.
Notice your breath. You don\'t need to change it.
Let your hands grow heavy.
Feel the bed holding you up.
Nothing to do now. Nothing to fix.
Let the day go.

resources.string: Required while Standby mode is on. You can hide this notification; Standby keeps working.
Used to show the screensaver over your lock screen. Never makes a sound.
Beddery will appear when you charge your phone
A dawn that rises over the 30 minutes before your alarm, lifting night mode and brightening the screen as the sky warms.
Set an alarm in your clock app and this screen will slowly brighten like dawn for half an hour before it rings.
Your bedroom window shows the town as the forecast says it\'ll be when you wake: a clear dawn, rain on the glass, snow on the roofs or a storm.
The real sky straight above you, framed by the treetops: bright stars, constellations, the planets and the Moon.
Estimated location · set one in Weather for accuracy
A lighthouse on a moonlit headland, its beam sweeping round every 14 seconds above the keeper\'s cottage. Tap to send a boat across.
The view from a sleeper compartment: a moonlit lake, a viaduct, villages and forest sliding past at their own speeds. Tap to rattle over the points.
Your cat asleep on a knitted blanket, moonlight from a round window on the wall behind. It breathes slowly; an ear flicks and the tail twitches. Choose its coat in the options.
Your screen is the glass of a planted tank: stone and driftwood, neon tetras, cherry shrimp, a toy diver, and now and then a showpiece fish. Tap to call one over.
Day, hour and minute glasses grouped like a still life, each draining over its span and turning over when it runs out. Tap to turn the minute glass.
A turned-wood hourglass under a spotlight that drains over each hour and turns itself over on the hour. Tap to turn it now.
A little pixel-art bedroom whose window, lamps and wall clock follow the real time of day.
Falling blocks that stack themselves into the time, then clear away and rebuild each minute.
